source_text: Nunc autem, cum nec exigua opinionis huius in Scripturis sanctis inveniatur occasio et e regione fides, quam tuemur, non minus rationibus suis quam exemplis et testimoniis muniatur, funesta es prorsus obstinatione pervasus, qui putas damno legis, damno rationis, damno prudentiae damnoque iustitiae Manichaeorum somniis annuendum.
pass_a_gloss: Now however, when not even a slight occasion of this opinion is found in the holy Scriptures and from the other side the faith which we guard is munited no less by its own reasons than by examples and testimonies, you have been altogether pervaded by a deadly obstinacy, who think that by loss of law, loss of reason, loss of prudence and loss of justice the dreams of the Manichaeans must be nodded to.

lemmas.lexica: Blaise Manichaeus; Julian's polemic label vs natural evil
LS ratio; Blaise use of reason required for sin

pass_b_english: But as it is, not even a slight occasion for this opinion can be found in the holy Scriptures. On the other side, the faith we defend is fortified by examples and testimonies no less than by its own reasons. You are therefore completely possessed by a deadly obstinacy, believing that Manichaean dreams must be accepted at the expense of law, reason, wisdom, and justice.

choices.why: Julian's standing charge: natural evil is Manichaean. Keep the sect-name, not 'dualists'.
Julian's forensic virtue that renders to each his own, without fraude or gratia (partiality).
rejected: righteousness (Pauline overlay unless the verse forces it)

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
